--- setup.sh ---
#! /usr/bin/env bash

set -e

if [ -n "$VIRTUAL_ENV" ]; then
    deactivate
fi

if [ -d .venv ]; then
    rm -rf .venv
fi

uv venv .venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install \
  "trl>=0.26" peft bitsandbytes accelerate \
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/v0.19.1/vllm-0.19.1+cu130-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl \
  reasoning-gym \
  datasets scipy matplotlib ipywidgets \
  --torch-backend=auto

# OpenEnv env servers (reasoning_gym and friends) are not on PyPI - they live in
# the meta-pytorch/OpenEnv repo and run as local HTTP servers. Agentic-mode
# training launches one as a subprocess, so clone the repo. Its path is read
# from training.env_server.repo_path in the config (default /workspace/OpenEnv/envs).
OPENENV_DIR="${OPENENV_DIR:-/workspace/OpenEnv}"
if [ ! -d "$OPENENV_DIR" ]; then
  git clone https://github.com/meta-pytorch/OpenEnv "$OPENENV_DIR"
fi

# Install the core from the same clone that provides the env servers, NOT the
# PyPI `openenv-core`. The two ship the same `openenv` import name, and a version
# skew between them fails at RUNTIME, not import time: the repo's env clients pass
# `metadata=` to `StepResult`, which older cores reject with a TypeError on the
# first reset. Installing both means whichever shadows the other decides the
# version, so `openenv-core` must be absent.
uv pip uninstall openenv-core 2>/dev/null || true
uv pip install -e "$OPENENV_DIR"

**No. Nothing pinned except the vllm wheel URL.** No `pyproject.toml`, no `requirements.txt`, no lockfile anywhere in repo.

`setup.sh` installs floating latest:
```
trl>=0.26 peft bitsandbytes accelerate reasoning-gym datasets scipy matplotlib ipywidgets
```
Only hard pin: `vllm-0.19.1+cu130` (URL). OpenEnv = `git clone` HEAD, editable-installed. Re-running `setup.sh` today gives a different stack than the box.

## What is actually on gpu-l4 (`.venv`, py 3.12.3)

| pkg | version |
|---|---|
| trl | **1.6.0** (spec said `>=0.26`) |
| transformers | 5.12.0 |
| torch | 2.10.0+cu130 |
| vllm | 0.19.1+cu130 (pinned) |
| peft | 0.19.1 |
| accelerate | 1.14.0 |
| bitsandbytes | 0.49.2 |
| reasoning-gym | 0.1.25 |
| datasets | 5.0.0 |
| numpy / scipy | 2.2.6 / 1.17.1 |
| browsergym-core / -miniwob | 0.14.3 |
| playwright | 1.44.0 |
| openenv | `-e file:///workspace/OpenEnv` |

OpenEnv clone: commit `024eedc9` = `v0.4.1-67-g024eedc`, Jul 31 2026.

## Three reproducibility holes

1. **OpenEnv unpinned AND dirty.** Box clone has uncommitted edits to `envs/finqa_env/server/{app,finqa_environment}.py` plus untracked `envs/mcp_databases/`. Even pinning the commit would not reproduce the box. finqa was deleted from the pipeline, so those edits are dead weight - but they prove the clone drifts.
2. **`setup.sh` does not build the box.** browsergym-core, browsergym-miniwob, playwright are installed on the box and used by every e30-e36 run, but appear nowhere in `setup.sh`. A fresh `./setup.sh` cannot run the browsergym campaign.
3. **No run records its stack.** `runs/<exp>/config.yaml` freezes the experiment config, not the dependency versions. e9-e36 all sit on "whatever was installed that week" - and trl is the library whose TIS/`sequence_mask` behaviour already bit you.

This violates the standing rule in ARCHITECTURE.md ("Pin versions and commit the lockfile"; "Builds are deterministic ... Never `latest`").

## Lazy fix (3 commands, ~5 min)

```bash
# 1. snapshot the box exactly as-is
ssh gpu-l4 'VIRTUAL_ENV=/workspace/master-thesis-code/.venv uv pip freeze' > requirements.lock.txt
# 2. pin OpenEnv in setup.sh: git -C "$OPENENV_DIR" checkout 024eedc9
# 3. setup.sh installs from the lock instead of the loose spec
```
Skipped: pyproject/uv.lock migration, per-run version stamping. Add per-run stamping when a result actually needs defending against a library change.

**Next steps:**
- Decide: commit `requirements.lock.txt` + pin OpenEnv to `024eedc9` in `setup.sh`? Say go and I do it.
- Decide whether the box's dirty finqa patches get reverted or committed somewhere (they are dead code now).
- Open question for the thesis writeup: e9-e36 have no recorded dependency versions. Lock now sets the floor for everything from the seed-43 replication onward.
go ahead, pin it and commit the lockfile and yes just revert the dead code and then only report to me the locked version for openenv for now

# sequence_mask, transformers' tool-call rendering) is a silent change to what
# the runs measure. Upgrade deliberately: install, verify, re-freeze the lock.
uv pip install -r requirements.lock.txt --torch-backend=auto
'''

#! /usr/bin/env bash

set -e

if [ -n "$VIRTUAL_ENV" ]; then
    deactivate
fi

if [ -d .venv ]; then
    rm -rf .venv
fi

uv venv .venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
# Every version comes from the lockfile, frozen off the GPU box. A floating
# install resolves a different stack every week, and a library change (trl's
# sequence_mask, transformers' tool-call rendering) is a silent change to what
# the runs measure. Upgrade deliberately: install, verify, re-freeze the lock.
uv pip install -r requirements.lock.txt --torch-backend=auto

# OpenEnv env servers (reasoning_gym and friends) are not on PyPI - they live in
# the meta-pytorch/OpenEnv repo and run as local HTTP servers. Agentic-mode
# training launches one as a subprocess, so clone the repo. Its path is read
# from training.env_server.repo_path in the config (default /workspace/OpenEnv/envs).
OPENENV_DIR="${OPENENV_DIR:-/workspace/OpenEnv}"
OPENENV_COMMIT="024eedc90305cc8bd7a5b44f44d1b987102e957b"  # v0.4.1-67-g024eedc
if [ ! -d "$OPENENV_DIR" ]; then
  git clone https://github.com/meta-pytorch/OpenEnv "$OPENENV_DIR"
fi
# Pin the clone too: it carries the env servers and their wire contract, so its
# HEAD is as load-bearing as any pinned wheel.
git -C "$OPENENV_DIR" fetch --quiet origin
git -C "$OPENENV_DIR" checkout --quiet "$OPENENV_COMMIT"

# Install the core from the same clone that provides the env servers, NOT the
# PyPI `openenv-core`. The two ship the same `openenv` import name, and a version
# skew between them fails at RUNTIME, not import time: the repo's env clients pass
# `metadata=` to `StepResult`, which older cores reject with a TypeError on the
# first reset. Installing both means whichever shadows the other decides the

playwright 1.44.0.

verify against a real reset, then re-freeze the lock in the same commit. A
version bump landing silently between two arms of a comparison confounds them
exactly like a geometry change would. Runs before this commit have no recorded
